data.description:
Our new Mac Book computers will now allow us to use Unity, the creative 2D/3D programming platform for creating Games and Multimedia applications. For those of you that wish to learn Unity may I ask that you start at the Essentials project please.              

https://learn.unity.com/learn/pathway/unity-essentials

We will be downloading this on to all the Mac Books as a starting point. If you want to do this on your computers at home, please download the Unity HUB and install the latest Unity Editor. It is best to have an account with Unity to keep track of your progress, so please ask a parent if you do not yet have an email account.

You can then download the Essentials Project from the link above and then Add it as a project from the Unity Hub application.

When you open the project from Unity Hub, you are guided through the missions.

Summary of Club Meeting on Wednesday 19th June

It was great to have Harrison back with us. He made a start on his web site using HTMl, CSS and javascript.

Similarly, Max added a second page to his website and had links that would take him to the other page when he clicked on an anchor tag

Natan started work on an API based flight data retrieval application, using Node/JS

Tomasz had somehow lost his installation of Visual Studio Code and so we spent quite sometime looking for it an eventually re-installing the software.

Aleks seems to have a few sprite animation issues with the explosions in his space invaders game but was able to sort out some of the issues.

Bill had enhanced his 2D platform game and demonstrated how to jump, rotate and bounce off spikes, blocks, conveyor belts and much more.

Summary of Club Meeting on Wednesday 12th June

A good week for sorting out 'bugs' in the members code.

Natan found why his SDR, Software Defined Radio, wasn't connecting to flight information services.
Max sorted out some resizing issues in his HTML image pictures of Liverpool Football team.
Bill is really quit adept at using Unity for his 3D program and he sorted out some physics effect that just didn't look right.
Aleks enhanced his sprite animations and sorted out some sizing issue in the explosion sequences.
Tomasz resolved his data issues and was able to use Plotly Express to draw pie charts, bar charts, line charts and scatter graphs.

Team work is always nice to see in action.
It was good to see Igor helping Max and others. 

I like the fact that we're using multiple programming languages
  Python        - Plotly Express and pygame space invaders
  C#              - Unity 2D platform game
  Java/Node - Software Defined Radio
  Javascript  - Displaying graphs
  HTML        -  Liverpool Football club web site

All in all a good meeting with members collectively fixing many issues and having cleaner, functioning code.

Summary of Club Meeting on Wednesday 5th June

Sounds like everyone had a good half term break and were keen to make progress on their projects.

Bill added some interesting physics to his Unity platform game. When the character jumped onto a conveyor belt it immediately started moving faster and if he jumped up and faced the opposite way to the motion of the belt the speed was clearly reduced. Great work Bill

Natan was working on "ethical" hacking. He has a friend who had created a website and wanted Natan to see how secure it was. Unfortunately it wasn't very secure because the api (access) key had been stored in a cookie which could be used to wreak havoc with the website.

Max was working on his Liverpool Football Club website. He updated several images and learnt how to resize them whilst also keeping the aspect ratio the same. It was nice to see Igor helping him out too. It's good to share thoughts.

Tomasz, and I, struggled to extend his graph plot app to draw Pi charts and not just histograms. I'll spend some time figuring out how it's done before the next club meeting.

Aleks worked on adding animations to his space invaders game and seemed to be making good progress.

Igor has taken an interest in some lidar based landscape simulations.
https://youtube.com/shorts/BxdQmoDNg2A?feature=shared
It'll be interesting to see how it progresses.

data.title: Home Assistant

message:
Summary of Club Meeting on Wednesday 22nd May

Max had finished his ping pong game, which was a python based game. In order to move on, Max started looking into creating web pages. He was able to use a template to create a website based on Liverpool football club. He created title, paragraph, table, and images elements. It was an impressive start to using HTML. His mum was happy too!

Somehow, Tomasz had got into a state where he could only run his graph plotting program if he started it with admin privileges. Once we realised the cause of the issue he was able to plot some bar charts without out much difficulty. He then started looking into how he could add a different function to the code to draw the same data as a pi chart. For home work he was tasked with sorting out the admin issue.

Aleks  added collision detection to his bullets and so handled them being destroyed, which in programmatic terms is a good skill to acquire. It doesn't sound much but it involves a lot of logic which typically catches a lot of programmers out.

Bill had some issues with his Unity based 2D platform game but he seemed to make some good progress.

Natan sorted out the IP issues he had last week, by updating the software and removing the fixed IP address. He's also looking into how to install Home Assistant on a Raspberry Pi to integrate with our weather station project.
Please note that there will be NO MEETING on Wednesday 29th May 🥲

Summary of Club Meeting on Wednesday 15th May

Stoo and Max finished adding a score, time and  player progress box to his ping pong game. Max also made it so that when te ball bounces of the bat it'll rebound  to a random angle.
h
There was still a lot of issues with the framework for Tomasz's graph plotting  which again meant that he didn't make as much progress on his weather plotting project as we would have liked to. However we did get the issues resolved and were able to try various combinations of metrics in  weather graphs.

Aleks  made it so that the aliens in his space invaders game could shoot back. That's another great step  forward,. At this rate he should be able to complete it by the end of June and along with that complete the project requirement of his Duke of Edinburgh award.

I'm not sure what Natan was working on but he seemed to have issues with internet connectivity and ended up changing various network settings. We were told that the centre had changed suppliers and to it was best to re-register the Wifi connection, but that didn't fix the issue. Other people were okay, so he kept trying to find the cause.

Bill is still going strong with his unity game called Darcy. He also submitted his work experience forms so that he could register an intent to work at my place for a week in July

In the last few moments of the meeting, Harrison and I made some changes to his ping pong game so that the ball didn't go through either bat. Basically we added more collision detection. He definitely needs to move on to a new project next meeting.

Summary of Club Meeting on Wednesday 8th May

Stoo and Max tackled adding a score, time and player progress box to his ping pong game.

Unfortunately, I underestimated how much more there was to do with the supporting graph plotting  framework, OpenAPI, which meant that Tomasz didn't make as much progress on his weather plotting project as we would have liked to.

Aleks introduced movement into his space invaders game. That's a great step forward, next will be collision detection or some refinement on the movement mechanics, such as moving he alien invaders closer to the player 'gun'. Great progress Aleks

Natan had been to Birmingham airport and was able to use his SDR dongle to capture about 20 minutes of flight tower communications, which he was very pleased about.

Bill is still going strong with his unity game called Darcy.

It was nice to have Harrison back and making progress, looks like he's about ready to move on to something more challenging

All in all a nice enjoyable meeting with members really making progress. Great to see

Summary of Club Meeting on Wednesday 1st May

Max made some good progress on changing the colour of the ball in his ping pong game.
He was able to merge in the logic for gradual colour changes and seemed happy with the outcome.
We'll tackle a score, time and  player progress box next week.

Tomasz was able to use github, the professional way of tracking code changes, to update the files on his laptop. He understands how the static data gets plotted and now needs to determine how to replace the static data with real weather station data.

Aleks introduced a second sprite/image into his invaders game and updated his DofE tracker spreadsheet.

Natan was working on using web pages and in particular the blank page to act as a proxy for his own content. He seemed to be making good progress and helped Max out with a few things.

Bill is still going strong with his unity game called Darcy. It's a pity Stoo couldn't make it because it would have been good to see how he'd integrated the Occulus VR headset into Bill's Darcy game.

It's definitely easier when Stoo is able to come.
But all in all, another good meeting.

Summary of Club Meeting on Wednesday 24th April

Max made some good progress on changing the colour of the ball in his ping pong game. He sparked some interest in Stoo and Igor when he wanted to go further and have the colour change gradually over time. There's been quite a few posts on our Discord server and we now have at least one solution.

Tomasz merged his code into a FastApi template and is now working on creating a UI, user interface, to ask the user to select which metrics, date ranges and plot type for his UK weather application which uses the met office data.

Aleks made some progress with his space invaders game. He learnt how to scale images to a size appropriate for having several alien spaceships on a line. One of the next steps would be to make them move.

Natan fine 'tuned' his SDR,  software defined radio, program which he'll be using in his flight simulator project.

Bill is still going strong with his unity game called Darcy. Stoo has been working on getting it sunning on his own PC and is   integrating it with his Oculus VR headset. It's nice to see that our club members are motivating us to join in.

All in all, a very good meeting.

Summary of 17th April Club Meeting

A really good meeting.

Stoo and Natan were looking further into SDR, software defined radio, in relation to Natan's flight simulation project and were able to get a clear signal by the end of the evening.

Bill's work on his Unity game has motivated Stoo to install Unity and Bill's game on his own PC with the intent of integrating it with his Occulus VR headset.

Max made good progress on his ping pong game. Stoo was able to test his understanding to make sure it wasn't just copy 'n' paste and he's really pleased with what Max was able to describe.

Aleks investigated the scaling of a large alien image and found out what happens when the PC runs low on memory, so we're looking into creating a range of scaled images as separate assets so that the game engine doesn't need to do any software scaling.

Tomasz, great progress, was able to install the various python modules to start using FastAPi. This working is getting really exciting and all the more valuable because it's a part of his Duke of Edinburgh award.

A summary of week ending 20th March

Great meeting, club members fully engaged.
It's really quite impressive what Bill is doing with his Unity game, he's on a roll and clearly getting more and more skilled with coding and Unity in general.
Natan was working on some airport simulation maps and had a basic design for a local airfield underway by the end of the meeting
Harrison and Max both separately made good progress on their ping pong game using python and pygame to good effect.
Aleks worked on creating a 'splash' screen for his invaders game.
Tomasz started working on the user interface for his weather mapping project and had integrated a very basic web page into the program.

All in all, a very rewarding and enjoyable evening

During our last session on  4th October, we coded games in python, C# and Unity and also dabbled with Discord 
Bots.
https://realpython.com/how-to-make-a-discord-bot-python/

Why not drop in on Wednesday 11th October to see what we are up to. The sessions are free and we usually have two STEM Ambassadors on hand to answer any questions and lend a helping hand with all matters code, where we can. If you have a laptop, please feel free to bring it along. We do have several desktop computers, a Mac Book and various embedded computing devices such as BBC Micro Bits and Raspberry Pi Pico.
